headings.title: Introduction and Definition of Dietetics
headings.content: Dietetics is the science and art of applying nutritional principles to regulate the human diet for health and disease management. Unlike general nutrition, which looks broadly at food and its biological uses, dietetics focuses on translating scientific knowledge into practical dietary guidance for individuals and groups. The field integrates biochemistry, physiology, and behavioral science to optimize human performance and clinical outcomes.

headings.title: Core Principles of Human Nutrition and Metabolism
headings.content: Human metabolism relies on macronutrients and micronutrients to sustain life. Macronutrients—carbohydrates, proteins, and fats—provide energy and building blocks for tissue repair. Micronutrients, consisting of vitamins and minerals, regulate metabolic pathways without yielding energy directly. A breakdown in metabolism, such as in diabetes mellitus, requires careful manipulation of these nutritional components to prevent severe clinical complications.

headings.title: The Role and Scope of Practice for a Dietitian
headings.content: A registered dietitian is a qualified healthcare professional who assesses, diagnoses, and treats nutritional problems. Their scope extends from ordering medical nutrition therapy in hospital wards to designing corporate wellness menus. Dietitians work alongside doctors and nurses to ensure that hospital patients receive feeds matching their metabolic demands.

headings.title: Clinical vs. Community Dietetics: Key Differences
headings.content:
Dietetics practice branches into distinct sectors based on the target population and environment.

- **Clinical Dietetics**: Focuses on individual patients in hospitals or clinics, managing disease-specific diets like renal or diabetic meal plans.
- **Community Dietetics**: Focuses on populations and public health, implementing nutrition programs, school feeding initiatives, and health education campaigns.

headings.title: The Nutrition Care Process (NCP) Framework
headings.content: The Nutrition Care Process is a systematic problem-solving method dietitians use to think critically and make decisions. It consists of four distinct steps: nutritional assessment, nutritional diagnosis, nutritional intervention, and nutritional monitoring and evaluation. This standardized framework ensures that patient care remains consistent, measurable, and effective across different healthcare environments.

headings.title: Dietetics in the Nigerian Healthcare Context
headings.content: In Nigeria, dietetics practice addresses a dual burden of malnutrition: undernutrition in rural areas alongside rising rates of diet-related chronic diseases in urban centers. Cultural food beliefs, economic factors, and reliance on local staples like cassava and yam shape how dietary advice is received. Dietitians in Nigerian hospitals must adapt international nutritional guidelines to fit locally available, affordable food items.

headings.title: Interprofessional Collaboration in Patient Care
headings.content: Optimal patient recovery depends on seamless communication between dietitians, nurses, physicians, and pharmacists. Nurses often observe daily dietary intake problems first, making their reports vital for the dietitian's reassessment. Collaborative ward rounds and shared electronic health records bridge gaps between disciplines, preventing conflicting medical instructions and improving patient safety.
